title: Volume 3 · Buying, Step by Step
subtitle: Lessons 1–4: the purchase cycle from order to payment, with the three quantities and three amounts that must match
outcomes: Raise a purchase order that purchasing and finance both accept
Receive goods so that stock and the stock-received account move together
Bill a supplier and explain the three-way match to an auditor
Pay the supplier and prove the creditor balance is back to zero

slides.title: Raise a purchase order finance can pay
bullets: A purchase order is a promise to a supplier, so the rate typed here is the rate that will be billed
Set the delivery date deliberately, because it drives the late-supplier list and the shortage report
Enter tax as a row in Purchase Taxes and Charges, never as a rounded-up rate in the item line
Submit only when the buyer and the budget owner agree, since submit locks quantity and rate

rows: Sunrise Components, group Local Suppliers, currency MYR
Supplier Sunrise Components, company Seri Murni Sdn Bhd
Address and currency fill from the supplier
SST Purchase 10 %, account SST Input - SM
Status becomes To Receive and Bill, 10 units pending

slides.notes: The commonest consultant error here is typing a rate that already includes tax, which inflates the stock value by ten per cent for the life of the item. Keep the item rate net, let the tax row do the adding, and the purchase receipt will post the correct stock value. Confirm the tax template before submitting, because changing a submitted order means amending it and reprinting.

slides.title: Read the purchase order before you submit it
bullets: Three numbers decide whether the order is right: net total, tax and grand total
A zero tax row usually means the supplier has no tax category, not that the item is exempt
The order must show zero stock effect, because nothing has physically moved yet
Print the order once and read it as the supplier will, including terms and delivery window

rows: Stock → Stock Ledger, filter voucher type Purchase Order

slides.notes: Ask the learner to compute the grand total before looking at the screen: ten units at 120 gives 1,200, ten per cent gives 120, and the total is 1,320. Being able to predict that figure is what separates a consultant from someone clicking through a demo. If the screen disagrees, the tax template or the supplier's tax category is wrong, and it is cheaper to find that now than at month end.

slides.title: Receive the goods and let stock move
bullets: The purchase receipt is the document that moves stock and posts the interim stock account
Receive into the warehouse that will hold the goods, not a generic default
Partial receipts are normal, so record what arrived rather than what was ordered
Do not create a stock entry to mimic a receipt, because the bill will never match

rows: Form pre-fills supplier, item and 10 units
Pending quantity falls to 0 on the order

slides.notes: Receipts post to Stock Received But Not Billed rather than to a creditor, which is why the balance sheet looks unusual between receipt and bill. That interim account is not an error and must not be cleared by hand: it clears itself when the invoice is submitted. Explain that to a client's accountant early, or they will journal against it and create a permanent difference.

slides.title: Prove the receipt moved stock, not profit
bullets: A receipt changes the balance sheet only: stock rises and an interim liability rises with it
The profit and loss account must be untouched at this point, because nothing has been sold
Valuation per unit is the purchase rate, adjusted later by any landed cost voucher
Serial and batch items need their numbers recorded at receipt, not after the bill

rows: Accounts → General Ledger, account Stock Received But Not Billed

slides.notes: If the profit and loss statement moves when you receive goods, an expense account has been configured as the default warehouse account, and every future valuation report will be wrong. Fix the default accounts in the Company record and the Warehouse record before going further. This is the single most common misconfiguration found during a first-week audit of a new ERPNext site.

slides.title: Bill the supplier and respect the three-way match
bullets: The bill brings the creditor into existence and clears the interim stock account
ERPNext will not let you bill more than you received, which is the control auditors ask about
Check the rate against the order, because a supplier invoice is not automatically correct
Set the payment due date from the template rather than typing a number

rows: Reference stored for the audit trail
Dr Stock Received Not Billed 1,200.00, Dr SST Input 120.00, Cr Creditors 1,320.00
Error: cannot bill more than received

slides.notes: The three-way match is the reason a purchase invoice cannot simply be typed from the supplier's paper. Order, receipt and bill must agree on quantity, and the rate is checked against the order. Show the learner the exact error message when they try to over-bill, because that message is the control working. Malaysian auditors frequently ask to see it demonstrated during system audits.

slides.title: The three-way match in numbers
bullets: Quantity, rate and total must agree across order, receipt and bill
Tax input sits as an asset account until the SST return is filed
The creditor balance is now a real liability with a due date and an ageing bucket
Nothing in the profit and loss moves until the goods are sold

rows: PO, PR and PI side by side

slides.notes: Get into the habit of opening the three documents side by side for the first purchase of any new client, because a mismatch there tells you whether their process will survive an audit. If the invoice was recorded without a receipt, the stock account will be overstated and the interim account will keep a credit balance that nobody can explain. Correct the process, not the ledger.

slides.title: Pay the supplier and close the loop
bullets: A payment entry against the invoice settles the creditor, and allocation is what makes it stick
Account Paid From and Bank Account (From) sit in Accounts and Transaction Details, not on a separate tab
The bank reference goes in Cheque/Reference No, which is what makes the reconciliation match later
Partial payment is normal: allocate what was paid and leave the rest outstanding
The invoice status changes to Paid only when the allocated amount equals the total

rows: Payment type Pay, party Sunrise Components
Bank account set on the payment

slides.notes: Allocation is the step learners skip. An unallocated payment leaves the invoice open, the ageing report wrong, and the client convinced the system is broken. Point out the two halves of the form as you teach it: Accounts and Transaction Details for the bank side, and the Reference table for the invoices being killed. Teach the rule as a sentence they can repeat: a payment is money in the bank, an allocation is the invoice it kills. If an invoice stays open after a payment, open Payment Reconciliation and allocate there.

slides.title: What each purchase document touches
bullets: Each document has exactly one job, and skipping one leaves a permanent trace
Order and bill are commitments, while receipt is the only one that moves stock
The interim account is a bridge, not a place to park corrections
Print the chain once per client so their accountant sees the logic before go-live

headers: What breaks if you skip it
rows: No control over rate or delivery date
Dr Stock, Cr Stock Received But Not Billed
Dr Stock Received, Dr SST, Cr Creditors
Cr Creditors, Cr Stock or expense

slides.notes: This table is the one-page answer to the question every client accountant asks in week one. Print it, put it next to the purchase desk, and mark the receipt line, because that is the document operations forget. When a client claims the stock value is wrong, walk this chain in order and the error is always in one of the four rows.

lab.title: Lab · Buy, receive, bill and pay ten blenders
steps: Create supplier Sunrise Components with Net 30 terms and the SST purchase category
Raise purchase order for 10 SM-BL200 at 120.00 with SST 10 % and confirm the 1,320.00 total
Compute the expected tax before submitting, then compare with the screen
Create the purchase receipt into Main warehouse and confirm bin quantity 10
Read the stock ledger row and confirm value 1,200.00 at 120.00 per unit
Create the purchase invoice, set the supplier reference and due date 15-02-2026
Attempt to bill 11 units on a copy and record the exact error message
Pay the invoice in full from the bank and confirm the invoice status is Paid
lab.done: Done when the creditor balance for Sunrise Components is zero, the bin at Main shows 10 units worth 1,200.00, and the stock ledger holds exactly one receipt row for this order.

quiz.question: Which document moves stock in the purchase cycle?
quiz.why: Only the purchase receipt creates stock ledger entries. The order is a commitment, the invoice creates the creditor, and the payment settles it.

quiz.question: What does a purchase receipt post to the credit side?
quiz.why: Receipts credit Stock Received But Not Billed, an interim liability that clears when the purchase invoice is submitted. Creditors appear only at invoice stage.

quiz.question: A purchase invoice for 11 units against a receipt of 10 will do what?
quiz.why: ERPNext blocks billing more than received by default, which is the control auditors test. It is configured in Buying Settings as allow over-billing.

quiz.question: An invoice stays open after a payment was submitted. What is the likely cause?
options: The payment was not allocated to the invoice
quiz.why: A payment reduces the creditor only when it is allocated against the invoice. Unallocated payments leave invoices open and ageing reports wrong.

quiz.question: Where do you confirm the valuation per unit after a receipt?
options: Stock Ledger row or Stock Balance report
quiz.why: The stock ledger row carries quantity, rate and value. Landed cost vouchers later adjust that value, which is why it belongs with valuation, not with purchasing.

narration: Buying is the mirror image of selling, and it is where most consultants lose credibility, because the client's accountant knows this cycle cold. Start with the purchase order: ten blenders at one hundred twenty, plus ten per cent tax, is one thousand three hundred twenty, and the order moves no stock. The receipt is the document that matters, adding ten units at one hundred twenty and crediting stock received but not billed, an interim account that looks strange and is not an error. The bill clears that account, brings in one hundred twenty of input tax, and creates a creditor of one thousand three hundred twenty with a due date. Then the payment, allocated to the invoice, closes it. Three documents, one quantity, one rate, one total. Teach the learner to predict the tax before looking, and to read the three documents side by side, because that habit is what survives an audit. When a client says the system is wrong, walk this chain in order and the answer appears in one of the four rows.
